premises.text: Contractor/vendor-heavy organizations need a formal system beyond spreadsheets
premises.evidence_span: we had no formalized way to handle this

premises.text: Internal searchable contractor index replaces informal discovery
premises.evidence_span: we've built these contractor cards of everyone. And now they're searchable and accessible by everyone in The Economist

premises.text: Templated onboarding collects day rates, remote/on-site, and signed terms
premises.evidence_span: what's your day rate? Are you available on-site or remote? or require them to sign the Economist Terms of Service

premises.text: Profiles surface prior internal feedback so institutional knowledge is not lost
premises.evidence_span: tracking who's good at what within an organization, like institutional knowledge, is always lost

premises.text: Projects create dual private/shared tracking and a single email-integrated thread
premises.evidence_span: we have one communication thread between the economist, her team, and the contributor. It's integrated with Gmail and Outlook

premises.text: System auto-collects performance feedback and invoices for scaled payment ops
premises.evidence_span: We'd also auto request that Patrick uploads his invoice

premises.text: Freemium SaaS distribution for any company to sign up free
premises.evidence_span: any company can sign up at our new website, listable.com, and use the product entirely for free

value.text: A new way of working together with external contributor networks
value.evidence_span: our company is facilitating a new way of working together
